To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the sovereign risk premium of a single country has a behavior consistent with the hypothesis of new market information, and that the Mexican crisis had a strong and permanent effect on risk premia in Mexico.

(1) the behavior of sovereign risk premias is not constant in time, (2) the Mexican crisis had a strong and permanent effect on sovereign risk assessment in Mexico, (3) the Mexican crisis generated a temporary effect on the sovereign risk assessment of other countries, and (4) the Mexican crisis increased the co-movement of sovereign risk premios.

(i) the behavior of risk premia in Brady bonds is consistent with the hypothesis of a unit root; (ii) there is evidence of co-movement in sovereign risk premia during the Mexican crisis, but no evidence of co-movements during a period of lower volatility; and (iii) the Mexican crisis had a strong, permanent effect on risk premia in Mexico, and a temporary effect on risk premias in Poland.
